$comment: Schema validation failures that are known, named, and deliberately not fixed in this release. tools/validate_corpus.py reports every entry on each run and does not fail on it; it DOES fail when an entry stops reproducing, so this file cannot rot into a blanket suppression list. Every entry is bound to error_signature, a deterministic fingerprint of the exact error it names, so a materially different failure at the same path, schema, JSON path and keyword is reported as an unregistered failure rather than inheriting this entry's excuse. A document listed here has NOT passed validation: the validator counts it under 'known', never under 'passed', and an instance document listed here cannot supply Level-3 evidence for its spec's promotion to Stable. Adding an entry requires an owning defect id, a justification, and a signature read off a real run (python3 tools/validate_corpus.py --signatures). It is not a place to park ordinary bugs.

fields.schema: schema file the failure comes from
fields.json_path: JSON Path of the failing instance location
fields.error_signature: SHA-256 over the error's structural shape: absolute schema path, failing keyword, that keyword's schema value, and recursively the same for every sub-error a composite keyword collected. Independent of instance values and of the rendered message, so unrelated frontmatter edits do not churn it — but a failure that changes shape at the same location no longer matches. Obtain it with: python3 tools/validate_corpus.py --signatures
fields.track: governance track that owns the fix (0 = PR + maintainer review, 1 = RFC per SPEC_LIFECYCLE.md)
fields.reason: why it is not fixed here

deviations.reason: Layer mismatch, not a document defect. contact.schema.json requires one of mcp_endpoint/api_endpoint/email/human_owner, which describes a deployed agent's contact card. specs/identity/CONTACT.md is the specification that defines those fields and correctly declares none of them. Closing it needs a normative decision — either split the per-spec schemas into a specification contract and an instance contract, or relax the anyOf on a Core-tier schema. Both are RFC-gated changes to a Core spec and are out of scope for the v1.3.2 maintenance release.
